Function: One of the Deuteronomy 13 safeguards against idolatry: do not take anything from an idolatrous city's spoil. The Law here is moral in its concern: conduct and character, not courtroom procedure. Scripture gives the reason: there shall cleave nought of the cursed thing to thine hand, that the LORD may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and shew thee mercy. The evil it addressed was profit from idolatry — keeping the spoil of a city destroyed for its gods. It restrained that evil by forbidding any gain from the purge: nothing of the cursed thing was to stick to Israel's hands. These civil penalties belonged to ancient Israel's theocracy; the refusal to follow idolatrous leading endures.
